'''Alexander Furman''' ({{Langx|he|אלכסנדר פורמן}}) is a mathematician at the [[University of Illinois at Chicago|University of Illinois]], Chicago.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.uic.edu/persisting_utilities/people/profile?netid=furman|title=Alexander Furman|website=www.math.uic.edu|access-date=February 13, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://today.uic.edu/2016-university-scholar-alexander-furman|title=2016 University Scholar Alexander Furman {{!}} UIC Today|website=today.uic.edu|access-date=February 13, 2020}}</ref> Furman received his bachelor's degree in mathematics and computer science from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 1986,<ref name="Alex Furman">{{Cite web|url=http://homepages.math.uic.edu/~furman/cv.html|title=Alex Furman|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref name="mathematics.huji.ac.il">{{Cite web|url=https://mathematics.huji.ac.il/home|title=Einstein Institute of Mathematics|website=mathematics.huji.ac.il|language=en|access-date=February 13, 2020}}</ref> later earning his master's degree and PhD in mathematics in 1989 and 1996, respectively, from the same university.<ref name="Alex Furman" /><ref name="mathematics.huji.ac.il" />

== Career ==
Furman started teaching mathematics in 1996 as an [[L. E. Dickson]] Instructor of Mathematics at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name="Alex Furman" /> In 1997, he received a position as a postdoctoral fellow at [[Penn State University]].<ref name="Alex Furman" />  He has worked at the [[University of Illinois Chicago]] since 1997, serving as an assistant professor from 1999 until 2007 and beginning as a full-time professor in 2007.<ref name="Alex Furman" /> Furman also runs the UIC Math Olympiad Project where he works with high school-age students, discussing and working out mathematical problems.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/uic.edu/uicmop|title=uicmop|website=sites.google.com|language=en-US|access-date=February 13, 2020}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Furman has been awarded multiple [[National Science Foundation Grant|National Science Foundation]]<ref name="Alex Furman" /><ref name="www.nsf.gov">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/|title=NSF – National Science Foundation|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=February 13, 2020}}</ref> and [[Binational Science Foundation]] grants.<ref name="Alex Furman" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bsf.org.il/|title=Homepage|website=BSF|language=en-US|access-date=February 13, 2020}}</ref> In 2014, Furman was made a [[Simons Foundation]] Fellow in Mathematics<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-mathematics/|title=Simons Fellows in Mathematics|last=|first=|date=|website=Simons Foundation|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref name="Alex Furman" /> and was awarded the [[National Science Foundation CAREER Award|National Science Foundation CAREER award]] for his work in teaching through research.<ref name="mscs.uic.edu">{{Cite web|url=https://mscs.uic.edu/faculty-awards/|title=Faculty Awards {{!}} Dept of Math, Stat, & Comp Sci {{!}} University of Illinois at Chicago|website=mscs.uic.edu|access-date=February 13, 2020}}</ref><ref name="www.nsf.gov" /> The same year, he was an invited speaker for the [[International Congress of Mathematics]] hosted in [[Seoul]].<ref name="mscs.uic.edu" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.icm2014.org/|title=International Congress of Mathematicians|website=www.icm2014.org|access-date=February 13, 2020}}</ref> For his work in [[dynamical system]]s, [[ergodic theory]], and [[Lie group]]s, he was made an [[American Mathematical Society]] Fellow in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/rnoti-p289.pdf|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|last=|first=|date=March 2016|website=American Mathematical Society|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> He has additionally received UIC's University Scholar Award, as well as the LAS Distinguished Professor Award.<ref name="mscs.uic.edu" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vpaa.uillinois.edu/academic_affairs_programs/univscholars|title=University Scholars Program – EVPAA|website=www.vpaa.uillinois.edu|access-date=February 13, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://las.uic.edu/about/administration/faculty-awards-research-support/|title=Faculty Awards & Research Support {{!}} College of Liberal Arts and Sciences {{!}}
